subject: scorpion
reasoning:
I'm planning a scorpion model using the SDK, trying to work conservatively from the limited API reference I have for joints, chains, sweeps, and parts, since I can't verify exact signatures. I'm reasoning through how joint parenting likely works, with the first joint being the root and subsequent joints referencing a parent.

To sidestep uncertainty around part orientation options like dir/aim/up, I'm opting to use raw three.js geometry transforms (rotating and translating the geometry myself) combined with a simple helper function for placing segments with position, bone, and rotation — a safer, more predictable approach. I'm also sketching out rough real-world scale dimensions for the scorpion's body and curled tail.

Planning out the full skeleton now: legs with coxa/knee/ankle joints, a segmented six-part tail ending in a stinger, and mesosoma segments, all laid out in centimeter coordinates facing +Z. I'm deciding on low-poly sphere and cylinder shapes for the carapace and abdomen segments to keep the blocky aesthetic while mapping out where each segment sits along the z-axis.

I'm working out the tail's curling arc as a sequence of joint positions, then writing a helper function that builds capsule-like rods between two points by orienting a cylinder along the connecting direction with a quaternion rotation — this will drive the legs, tail, and claw geometry uniformly. Now I'm positioning the four leg pairs along the body's sides, defining where each coxa segment starts.

Continuing to the pedipalps, I'm placing the arm, elbow, wrist, and pincer joints out front of the head, plus small chelicerae boxes and eye spheres on the carapace. I'm also picking out the color palette (sandy amber shell, dark brown accents, black eyes) and planning tergite plate details and ridged, tapering tail segments ending in a bulbous stinger with a curved spike, before setting up a mirrored loop to duplicate everything symmetrically on both sides.

Now I'm writing the helper functions for building each mesh part — converting positions into scaled coordinates, adding ellipsoid shapes for body segments, and constructing tapered rod/cylinder bones oriented between two joint points...

Placing pincer geometry...

Adjusting the fixed finger position to avoid crossing the palm width, then mapping out the arm joints from shoulder to elbow to wrist, with the palm positioned at the wrist's end using appropriate ellipsoid radii.

Checking overall body dimensions—roughly 28cm long and 14cm tall with the tail extending back—then finalizing the structure to return the root node, setting up metadata export, and grounding the legs so feet sit at y=0.
